study type: Prospective observational study and interrupted time-series analysis with a historical control cohort
exposure: Implementation of an operative vaginal birth safety bundle (including routine intrapartum ultrasound, a structured time-out and procedural checklist, birth experience survey, and a postnatal debrief pathway)
outcome: Neonatal composite morbidity (Apgar score <7 at 5 minutes, cord lactate >8 mmol/L, severe birth trauma, intubation or cardiac compressions, therapeutic cooling, and NICU admission)
Neonates delivered in an unexpected position
Cesareans without attempted operative vaginal birth
Births with >=4 tractions or >=2 cup detachments
Cesarean for unsuccessful operative vaginal birth
cohort: All women having an operative vaginal birth or fully dilated cesarean of a term singleton cephalic nonanomalous fetus at Monash Health.
finding: Implementation of a safety bundle for operative vaginal birth reduced the rates of unsuccessful operative vaginal birth and may reduce rates of severe neonatal birth trauma and neonatal intensive care unit admissions, without significant differences in the predefined composite neonatal morbidity or overall maternal morbidity.
mod_finding: The safety bundle implementation led to more cesareans without attempted operative vaginal birth, fewer births with >=4 tractions or >=2 cup detachments, less unsuccessful operative vaginal births, and significant step reductions in fully dilated cesarean and unsuccessful operative vaginal birth attempts.
